title: Sprint 5 - PL/pgSQL Programmatic Logic, Triggers & Exceptions

tickets.title: Audit History Triggers
tickets.description: Creates a PL/pgSQL function and trigger to write old balance changes to audit logs whenever account balances are updated.
tasks: Creates a PL/pgSQL function and trigger to write old balance changes to audit logs whenever account balances are updated.
learning_objectives: Understand relational database design and PostgreSQL features.
tickets.evaluation: `check_trigger_exists("trg_audit_balance")` `verify_audit_log_written_on_balance_update()` **[A] Correctness (40 pts)**: 40 pts if trigger inserts logs on balance changes. **[B] Optimality (30 pts)**: 30 pts for JSONB serialization execution. **[C] Quality (20 pts)**: 20 pts for returning the correct `NEW` node in PL/pgSQL.
common_mistakes: Forgetting semicolons at the end of statements.
Using reserved keywords as column names without quotes.
hints: Remember to use GROUP BY for aggregate functions like SUM, COUNT, or AVG.

tickets.title: Custom Exchange Conversion Function
tickets.description: Writes a PL/pgSQL database function that takes standard amount, base currency, and target currency, returning converted values.
tasks: Writes a PL/pgSQL database function that takes standard amount, base currency, and target currency, returning converted values.
learning_objectives: Understand relational database design and PostgreSQL features.
tickets.evaluation: `check_function_exists("convert_currency")` `verify_function_output("convert_currency(100, 'USD', 'EUR')", 92.00)` **[A] Correctness (40 pts)**: 40 pts if conversions return correct decimals. **[B] Optimality (30 pts)**: 30 pts for branch lookup speed. **[C] Quality (20 pts)**: 20 pts for declaring explicit typed variables.
common_mistakes: Forgetting semicolons at the end of statements.
Using reserved keywords as column names without quotes.
hints: Review the PostgreSQL documentation for exact syntax.
Test your queries in smaller chunks first.

tasks: Writes a stored procedure to transfer cash between accounts, wrapping operations in exceptions checks to rollback on insufficient funds.
